audit.whatIsWrong: Three lines tell the player to Wind Wall Sett's R, his W, or his 'R-landing autos'.
audit.why: Sett has no projectile anywhere in his kit — Q is an auto-attack empower, W is a cone punch, E is a pull, R is point-and-click. Wind Wall is a non-interaction here. The mirror audit found six such instructions on the Sett side and removed them all.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the interaction that does exist: Facebreaker (E) stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides of him — from one side it is just a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker's one-side / two-side rule is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' That is a positioning rule the player can act on every trade.
audit.corrected: Stay on one side of Sett — his E slows instead of stunning, and his stun-into-W combo never starts.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns; Haymaker described only as 'shield + true damage'.
audit.why: Knuckle Down 9s at rank 1, Haymaker 18s at rank 1 down to 12s, Facebreaker 16s at rank 1, The Show Stopper 120/100/80s. Haymaker's size scales with the damage YOU deal him, which is why a long trade is self-defeating.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, early and mid, with the Grit-banking mechanic stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4-5, first item and 2+ items read Skill.
audit.why: The already-audited sett side settled on Sett through first item and Yasuo at 2+ items; a 45.62% win rate agrees that the lane phase is his.
audit.corrected: Rows aligned in matched full/content pairs with ratings.

audit.why: packet suspectName 'Show Stopper' is a FALSE POSITIVE — the full Riot name is The Show Stopper and the text uses it correctly elsewhere.

edits.before: With two crit items you kite, wall, and out-scale his brawl kit.
edits.after: With two crit items you kite and out-scale his brawl kit.

edits.before: The Show Stopper (R) suplex is a point-and-click displacement that sets up a guaranteed W-stun combo; his all-in is already winning, so avoid giving him a target-rich fight where he can ult you into his team.
edits.after: The Show Stopper (R) is a 120s point-and-click suplex — no skillshot to sidestep and nothing to block, so hold Flash for the moment he commits and never fight him anywhere he can throw you into his team.

edits.before: You out-scale Sett past two crit items: at 100% crit you kite his gap-close, Wind Wall the Show Stopper (R) landing autos and his W punch, and out-DPS him once his combo is spent.
edits.after: You out-scale Sett past two crit items: at 100% crit you kite his gap-close, stay on one side of him so Facebreaker (E) only slows, and out-DPS him once his combo is spent.

edits.before: Sett bullies levels 1-3: his passive right-punch and Knuckle Down (Q) out-damage you in melee, and Haymaker (W) stores your trade damage into a true-damage counter-punch while his grit shield absorbs your Steel Tempest (Q) poke.
edits.after: Sett bullies levels 1-3: Knuckle Down (Q, 9s at rank 1) puts max-health damage on two punches, and Haymaker (W) banks the damage you deal him and returns it as true damage, so poke and leave instead of standing in his Q window.

edits.before: He stays ahead through levels 4-6 — his brawl kit sustains through your trades, and The Show Stopper (R) at 6 gives him a point-and-click suplex into a W-stun combo that makes his all-in nearly unbeatable, so farm safe and don't feed his W.
edits.after: He stays ahead through levels 4-6 — Haymaker (W, 15s at rank 3) banks the damage you deal him and returns it as true damage, and Facebreaker (E, 13s) stuns only when you are on the far side of him, so trade from inside the wave, on one side.

edits.before: Sett is a lane bully who scales worse than you; once you reach two crit items you kite his gap-close, Wind Wall his R-landing autos and Haymaker punch, and out-DPS him the moment his brawl combo is on cooldown.
edits.after: Sett is a lane bully who scales worse than you; once you reach two crit items you kite his gap-close, keep off both sides of him so Facebreaker only slows, and out-DPS him the moment his combo is down.

edits.before: Save Wind Wall for his Show Stopper (R) or Haymaker (W) in the all-in
edits.after: Stay on one side of him so Facebreaker (E) slows instead of stunning

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Haymaker: 18s at rank 1 — it banks the damage you deal him, so a long trade arms it for him. - Facebreaker: 16s at rank 1, stuns only from opposite sides. - The Show Stopper: 120s at rank 1, point-and-click.

edits.before: Sett wastes Haymaker — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns only from the far side — stay on one side.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Every point you deal into him is banked into Haymaker's punch.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: Shield + true damage. Bait it. When it is down — EQ-R him.
edits.after: Haymaker banks your damage. Facebreaker stuns only from both sides — stay one side.

notes: UNVERIFIED, deliberately not asserted: the kit file puts a 'grounding' flag on The Show Stopper, but Riot's own description says only carry-slam plus a slow, so I did not write that his R shuts off your E or Last Breath.
